text:
sara.support: :wave: Heads up — ACME reported a spike of 429s from EU (eu-west-1) around 2025-11-03T10:22Z. After a couple minutes the traffic got routed to US-west and started failing with 403 (IP allowlist). Customer says this cause major latency/billing anomalies. Can oncall confirm how cross-region failover works and recommended mitigations? cc @mike.sre @nina.eng

mike.sre: thanks. can you paste a minimal repro (curl + headers) and one request_id from the trace? also want to know if account has regional affinity enabled.

sara.support: repro + sample response attached below. request_id: req_0a7c3b. account: acme-inc. affinity looks default (not forced).
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"input":"short prompt"}'
```
Response sequence (timestamps approximate):
- 2025-11-03T10:22:07Z -> 429  {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":1.2} 
- 2025-11-03T10:22:09Z -> 200 (routed to us-west) but body: 403 Forbidden (IP not allowlisted) 
- From customer logs: repeated reconnects -> lots of retries -> billing increase.

infra-bot: [autoscan] Observed cluster: eu-west-1 capacity exhaustion window 10:22:06Z-10:25:00Z. Failover policy: allow_cross_region_fallback = true for account acme-inc. Burst credits remaining: 0.65/1.00. Regional affinity TTL = 300s. Routing header captured: X-Routed-Region: us-west-2.

nina.eng: key notes — our failover logic is: if regional queue is saturated we will attempt fallback to compatible region (matching model family). That is controlled by allow_cross_region_fallback and by account-level affinity TTL. With affinity TTL=300, clients without explicit affinity can be drifted after TTL expires. Looks like EU saturated -> fallback -> customer side blocked by IP allowlist on us-west.

qa-eli: repro steps I used locally:
1) set header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1
2) hammer at 150 rps for 30s with small payloads
3) watch for initial 429s then subsequent 302-like routing (we return X-Routed-Region).
Logs to collect if you escalate: X-Request-Id, X-Routed-Region, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Burst-Credits, and full response bodies.

nina.eng: recommended mitigations:
- short term (minutes): add us-west-2 IP(s) to the customer's allowlist so fallback succeeds; or temporarily disable cross-region fallback per-account:
```
PATCH /v1/accounts/acme-inc/config
Authorization: Bearer sk-admin
{ "allow_cross_region_fallback": false }
```
- medium term: bump regional_affinity_ttl or increase eu-west burst credits for the account if workload is bursty.
- long term: advise customer to set strong regional_affinity or pin allowed_regions in their SDK call so requests don't cross into restricted infra.

mike.sre: agree. operational plan:
1) sara/support to ask customer permission to whitelist two IPs for us-west-2 for 24-48h (fastest).
2) if they decline, we can toggle allow_cross_region_fallback=false for the account and monitor.
3) eng to provision a short EU capacity top-up if they want to keep fallback on.

cs-liz: reached out to ACME, they agreed to a temporary IP whitelist for us-west-2 until next Monday. They've asked for an internal postmortem and a clear checklist to avoid billing surprises.

sara.support: applying whitelist now (please monitor). I also uploaded the customer's raw request samples and request_id to the support ticket.

mike.sre: thanks. For diagnostics, if you see repeated 429 -> fallback -> 403 sequences, collect a 3-minute window of request headers and include tokens consumed. I'll escalate to capacity if we see sustained saturation.

qa-eli: small note — SDKs can set header `X-Redwood-No-Fallback: true` to opt out per-request if they need absolute regional affinity. forwarding this to docs team as well.

infra-bot: [action] Created incident INC-2025-7215 (eu-west burst). Assigned to @mike.sre and @nina.eng.

sara.support: closing loop — customer whitelisted us-west IPs, traffic normalized after ~12 minutes, no further 403s. We'll follow up with ACME on recommended configuration (regional_affinity_ttl 1800 + increase burst credits) and produce a short postmortem. :white_check_mark:
